questions.question: Explain the difference between a primary and a secondary source, giving an example of each related to Mali, and explain why historians compare several sources.
questions.expected_answer: A primary source comes from the time studied, e.g. an eyewitness traveller's account of Mali or a manuscript from Timbuktu. A secondary source is written later about the past, e.g. a modern textbook on Mali. Historians compare sources because any one source may be biased, incomplete or mistaken, and comparing shows different perspectives.

questions.question: Describe four ways in which the camel is adapted to desert conditions.
questions.expected_answer: Can go a week or more without drinking and then drink large amounts quickly; hump stores fat for energy; broad padded feet do not sink in sand; long eyelashes, hairy ears and closable nostrils keep out sand; eats thorny dry plants; loses little water.

questions.question: Explain why trans-Saharan traders travelled in caravans and why the guide was so important.
questions.expected_answer: Travelling together gave protection against raiders and allowed traders to share water, supplies, guides and knowledge. The guide knew the routes and the locations of wells and oases and navigated by the stars and landscape; missing a well could mean death for the whole caravan.
